failure_modes.name: Missing_Evidence_Not_Specified
failure_modes.evidence: Summary 1: 'The passages do not contain information about an athlete who was drafted, played for the Jets two years later, and was specifically re-acquired in the 2015 New York Jets season.' Summary 2: 'No athlete in the passages matches all the specified criteria of being drafted, playing for the New York Jets two years after the draft, and being re-acquired specifically in the 2015 New York Jets season.' Neither summary names which specific athlete or entity to search for regarding 2015 re-acquisition.

failure_modes.name: Query_Form_Mismatch
failure_modes.evidence: Query 2: 'Which athlete was re-acquired by the New York Jets in 2015 after being drafted and playing elsewhere?' - This is a natural-language yes/no question format. Query 3: 'Which athlete was re-acquired by the New York Jets in the 2015 season, when was he originally drafted, and did he play for the Jets two years after being drafted?' - This is a compound multi-part question bundling three separate targets.

failure_modes.name: Query_Stagnation
failure_modes.evidence: Query 2: 'Which athlete was re-acquired by the New York Jets in 2015...' and Query 3: 'Which athlete was re-acquired by the New York Jets in the 2015 season...' Both queries ask essentially the same core question about re-acquisition in 2015, with only minor rephrasing and additional sub-questions in query 3. The retrieval results show repeated documents (Kris Jenkins, Tom Draper, Justin Miller, Devin Smith appear multiple times across hops).

failure_modes.name: Evidence_Present_But_Missed
failure_modes.evidence: The Justin Miller passage states: 'He played for the Jets from 2005 to 2008, the Oakland Raiders from 2008 to 2009, the Jets again in 2009'. Miller was drafted by the Jets in 2005, played immediately (not two years later, so claim is false on that point), but WAS re-acquired in 2009. The solver's summary 1 mentions Miller's 2009 return but fails to clearly state this refutes the '2015 re-acquisition' portion of the claim - the evidence to refute is present but the solver treats it as insufficient rather than refutational.
